title: Suppressing CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma Axis Facilitates Neuronal Replacement and Synaptogenesis by Human Neural Precursor Grafts and Improves Recovery after Spinal Cord Injury.
authors: Hosseini, Seyed Mojtaba; Alizadeh, Arsalan; Shahsavani, Narjes; Chopek, Jeremy; Ahlfors, Jan-Eric; Karimi-Abdolrezaee, Soheila
journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
one_liner_zh: 该文研究脊髓损伤后CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma轴对神经前体细胞移植分化和突触形成的影响，属于神经再生与细胞治疗领域，不涉及蛋白质-DNA互作或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) is a leading cause of permanent neurologic disabilities in young adults. Functional impairments after SCI are substantially attributed to the progressive neurodegeneration. However, regeneration of spinal-specific neurons and circuit re-assembly remain challenging in the dysregulated milieu of SCI because of impaired neurogenesis and neuronal maturation by neural precursor cells (NPCs) spontaneously or in cell-based strategies. The extrinsic mechanisms that regulate neuronal differentiation and synaptogenesis in SCI are poorly understood. Here, we perform extensive in vitro and in vivo studies to unravel that SCI-induced upregulation of matrix chondroitin sulfate proteoglycans (CSPGs) impedes neurogenesis of NPCs through co-activation of two receptor protein tyrosine phosphatases, LAR and PTPsigma. In adult female rats with SCI, systemic co-inhibition of LAR and PTPsigma promotes regeneration of motoneurons and spinal interneurons by engrafted human directly reprogramed caudalized NPCs (drNPC-O2) and fosters their morphologic maturity and synaptic connectivity within the host neural network that culminate in improved recovery of locomotion and sensorimotor integration. Our transcriptomic analysis of engrafted human NPCs in the injured spinal cord confirmed that inhibition of CSPG receptors activates a comprehensive program of gene expression in NPCs that can support neuronal differentiation, maturation, morphologic complexity, signal transmission, synaptic plasticity, and behavioral improvement after SCI. We uncovered that CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma axis suppresses neuronal differentiation in part by blocking Wnt/beta-Catenin pathway. Taken together, we provide the first evidence that CSPGs/LAR/PTPsigma axis restricts neurogenesis and synaptic integration of new neurons in NPC cellular therapies for SCI. We propose targeting LAR and PTPsigma receptors offers a promising clinically-feasible adjunct treatment to optimize the efficacy and neurologic benefits of ongoing NPC-based clinical trials for SCI.SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT Transplantation of neural precursor cells (NPCs) is a promising approach for replacing damaged neurons after spinal cord injury (SCI). However, survival, neuronal differentiation, and synaptic connectivity of transplanted NPCs within remain challenging in SCI. Here, we unravel that activation of chondroitin sulfate proteoglycan (CSPG)/LAR/PTPsigma axis after SCI impedes the capacity of transplanted human NPCs for replacing functionally integrated neurons. Co-blockade of LAR and PTPsigma is sufficient to promote re-generation of motoneurons and spinal V1 and V3 interneurons by engrafted human caudalized directly reprogramed NPCs (drNPC-O2) and facilitate their synaptic integration within the injured spinal cord. CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma axis appears to suppress neuronal differentiation of NPCs by inhibiting Wnt/beta-Catenin pathway. These findings identify targeting CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma axis as a promising strategy for optimizing neuronal replacement, synaptic re-connectivity, and neurologic recovery in NPC-based strategies.
abstract_zh:
创伤性脊髓损伤（SCI）是年轻人永久性神经功能障碍的主要原因。SCI后的功能损伤主要归因于进行性神经退行性变。然而，在SCI失调的微环境中，由于神经前体细胞（NPCs）自发或基于细胞策略中的神经发生和神经元成熟受损，脊髓特异性神经元的再生和回路重建仍具挑战性。调控SCI中神经元分化和突触发生的外在机制尚不清楚。在此，我们进行了广泛的体外和体内研究，揭示SCI诱导的基质硫酸软骨素蛋白聚糖（CSPGs）上调通过共激活两种受体蛋白酪氨酸磷酸酶LAR和PTPsigma阻碍NPCs的神经发生。在成年雌性大鼠SCI模型中，系统性共抑制LAR和PTPsigma可促进移植的人直接重编程尾侧化NPCs（drNPC-O2）再生运动神经元和脊髓中间神经元，并促进其形态成熟及在宿主神经网络中的突触连接，最终改善运动功能和感觉运动整合的恢复。我们对损伤脊髓中移植人NPCs的转录组分析证实，抑制CSPG受体可激活NPCs中一套全面的基因表达程序，该程序可支持SCI后的神经元分化、成熟、形态复杂性、信号传递、突触可塑性和行为改善。我们发现CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma轴部分通过阻断Wnt/β-Catenin通路抑制神经元分化。综上所述，我们提供了首个证据表明CSPGs/LAR/PTPsigma轴限制了NPC细胞疗法中SCI新神经元的神经发生和突触整合。我们提出靶向LAR和PTPsigma受体是一种有前景的临床可行辅助治疗策略，可优化基于NPC的SCI临床试验的疗效和神经获益。

意义声明 移植神经前体细胞（NPCs）是脊髓损伤（SCI）后替代受损神经元的一种有前景的方法。然而，在SCI中，移植NPCs的存活、神经元分化和突触连接仍具挑战性。在此，我们揭示SCI后硫酸软骨素蛋白聚糖（CSPG）/LAR/PTPsigma轴的激活阻碍了移植人NPCs替代功能整合神经元的能力。共阻断LAR和PTPsigma足以促进移植的人尾侧化直接重编程NPCs（drNPC-O2）再生运动神经元和脊髓V1和V3中间神经元，并促进其在损伤脊髓中的突触整合。CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma轴似乎通过抑制Wnt/β-Catenin通路抑制NPCs的神经元分化。这些发现确定靶向CSPG/LAR/PTPsigma轴是优化基于NPC策略中神经元替代、突触再连接和神经恢复的有前景策略。
